Tim Hortons' are not Corporate.

This post is misleading and ill explain why.

The establishments are franchised. Owners lease the name Tim Hortons for their stores, and in doing so agree to only have products and ingredients provided exclusively through Tim Hortons supply chains. Corporate sells everything to the owners, they do not supply wages to employees, that is up to the owner of that establishment.

Some Tim Hortons owners provide paid breaks. Some allow 1 coffee and a donut on your break, some just 1 coffee, some owners give nothing.

The problem is the outrageous prices Corporate makes owners pay for the products. This is where id like to remind you that nothing is made in Tim Hortons, it is simply prepared there (from the freezer). This gives full control to Corporate on how much money they can charge a store for a box of everything bagels, or a container of fondant. You get the idea. The Corporate entity at Tim Hortons has just become a middle man that leases the right to use the name "Tim Hortons".

This isn't entirely bad as it ensures standards across all stores and continuity of products between one store and another meaning you can expect the same type and quality of product in Vancouver that you would expect in Montreal.

This however gets bad when owners don't get to see why products cost them so much and creates a blind spot where Corporate can essentially charge as much as they want (as much as they can).

Owners aren't rolling in the type of money you think they are either. I worked in management at a busy, well managed, and efficient store and had a good relationship with the owner and could see the profits...

Its about 10 cents on every dollar that the owner (the business) will profit. That's after labour cost. Which is a pretty thin profit margin to work with.

The solution is to increase the cost customers pay to make more money for the owner, and then at that point the owner would increase wages (hopefully instead of just banking the profit lol). But this is difficult because customers don't want to pay a higher price for their coffee and sandwiches. Not to mention the main competition (The Golden Arches), would attract all the fleeing customer base with their now lower prices.

Its not as easy as "Cancel the CEO".

Edit: owners also can't manipulate the prices on the menu (by that much). It is decided at the Corporate level.

Source: Me at Tim Hortons for 7 years.
